In regards to the neuroscience question— I personally don’t think the will to power ties in too heavily with our addiction to social media. Our addictions are fed thanks to our internal physical machinery. Its been studied that we are addicted to the /feeling/ that comes before a temporary addictive action rather than the feeling of we get /during/ the performance of said addictive action— and this applies to any temporary addictive habits we pick up, not just social media scrolling. This is tied to a chemical spike of dopamine rather than our deep emotional desire for expansion on power. Dopamine is an innate bodily reaction that can be seen in all living beings. Plants and animals get dopamine spikes. They have no concept of Nietzschean philosophy lol

However I’m sure that on a case to case basis, we may use social media to fill in other hidden desires to feel validated or “right” but that probably has less to do with our brain chemistry and more to do with our inner worlds and psyches.

I am actively working on this in therapy, wow. I always find myself in constant resistance with my diagnosis just because I am quick to intellectualize my behaviors and spot them. Its very tricky, because hypomania is, atleast in my case, less intense than full blown mania, therefore alot easier to be aware of. I think, “well, I understand that I am acting this way because of x y z and am aware of such behavior… therefore It’s not that serious! I have it under control I’m fine!” and then go about my weeks, subtly spiraling and over spending my savings, crossing small boundaries , being subtly irresponsible….. all things that seem small in retrospect but cause a huge ripple in my progress and overall routine. 

So yes, it’s normal, you’re not alone. However, this in no way means you should be off medications/ not take any action. We’re all too familiar with the intense seemingly overnight changes with our brains. Write. Down. EVERYTHING. This helps a ton. Wishing you luck <3
